necessary_context.content: There are N strategies. On trial t the allocator selects p^t with nonnegative coordinates summing to one, then receives a loss vector ell^t in [0,1]^N and incurs p^t dot ell^t. Loss vectors may depend on the allocator's current p^t. L_A=sum_{t=1}^T p^t dot ell^t and L_i=sum_{t=1}^T ell_i^t.
necessary_context.locator: PDF/printed p.2, online allocation model and cumulative-loss definitions
necessary_context.name: Online allocation and mixture loss

necessary_context.content: Figure 1 permits nonnegative initial weights summing to one, including zero weights, and displays beta in [0,1]. This extraction selects 0<beta<1 so normalization stays defined and Equation (7) has a positive denominator and finite log beta. A finite singleton comparison additionally requires the compared strategy's initial weight to be positive; other initial weights may be zero.
necessary_context.locator: PDF/printed p.4, Figure 1 and Section 2; p.6, Theorem 2 Equation (7)
necessary_context.name: Initial weights and selected beta regime

necessary_context.content: W_t=sum_j w_j^t. Lemma 1 gives ln W_{T+1} <= -(1-beta)L_H. Equation (6) gives w_i^{T+1}=w_i^1 beta^{L_i}; these supply the upper and lower bounds on the same potential used in Theorem 2.
